commitResults.messageTitle: Updating the initial code to simply greet the user and exit
Update code to echo commands entered by user and exit when user types command bye
Add ability to store whatever text the user enters and display it back when requested
Implement the mark command to update task status, without using additional classes

commitResults.messageBody: Introduce a TaskList abstraction to own task storage and common collection operations. Update Plana and Storage to use the abstraction so the command loop no longer depends directly on ArrayList while preserving the existing persistence and console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract console interaction handling into Ui
commitResults.messageBody: Move scanner ownership, startup and exit messages, help output, command echoing, error display, and separator formatting out of Plana. Keep command-specific task responses in Plana so this incremental refactoring preserves the existing console contract while establishing a dedicated UI boundary.

Complete the current UI extraction by moving task listing, date-query headings, empty-query messages, and add/delete/mark confirmations out of Plana. Keep task filtering and state changes in the command loop while centralizing all console rendering in Ui without changing the user-visible output.

Centralize command-type recognition and argument extraction in Parser. Update Plana to consume ParsedCommand so repeated command-prefix slicing is removed while retaining existing validation, execution, and console behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move task creation parsing into Parser
commitResults.messageBody: Centralize ToDo, Deadline, and Event syntax validation plus date conversion in Parser. Keep Plana focused on constructing tasks, updating the task list, saving changes, and presenting responses without changing the console behavior.

Make TaskList responsible for validating user-facing task numbers and performing delete, mark, and unmark operations. Keep Plana focused on dispatching commands, saving changes, and presenting the resulting task responses without changing console behavior.

Add the abstract Command execution contract and extract the bye behavior into ExitCommand. Route Plana's exit handling through the new command type while preserving the existing command loop and console behavior for all other commands.
Move the help and task-list responses into HelpCommand and ListCommand. Keep Plana's command loop and all console output unchanged while extending the executable Command hierarchy.

Move date formatting, deadline and event matching, empty-result handling, and query responses into OnCommand. Keep Plana responsible only for parsing the query date and delegating execution without changing console behavior.
Move task deletion, persistence, and deletion feedback into DeleteCommand. Keep Plana focused on parsing and dispatching while preserving existing validation and console behavior.
Move task completion, persistence, and confirmation feedback into MarkCommand. Keep Plana focused on parsing and dispatching while preserving existing validation and console behavior.
Move task unmarking, persistence, and confirmation feedback into UnmarkCommand. Keep Plana focused on parsing and dispatching while preserving existing validation and console behavior.
Centralize task insertion, persistence, and confirmation feedback in AddCommand for ToDos, deadlines, and events. Preserve Parser validation and all existing console behavior.
Move command construction and input error command creation into Parser so Plana only reads, executes, and observes exit commands. Preserve all existing parsing errors and console transcripts.

Give Storage an instance-owned data path with a configurable constructor and route startup and state-changing commands through that instance. Preserve the default data/plana.txt location and existing persistence behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes under a single plana package
commitResults.messageBody: Keep src/main/java as the source root while matching package declarations to the new plana directory. Update documentation and test launchers to use the package-qualified entry point.

Group commands, tasks, parsing, storage, UI, and exceptions into separate packages while keeping Plana in the root package. Preserve the source root and existing runtime behavior as the class count grows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add task model and collection tests
Add command type and UI tests

commitResults.messageBody: Use ASCII-only skill metadata and instructions so the Windows validator can read the files with its default encoding after PyYAML is made available.

Users need a way to locate tasks by words in their descriptions.

Add command parsing, case-insensitive description matching, result
formatting, help guidance, and focused tests for successful and empty
searches.

The UI test plan must describe every user-visible command and its
expected transcript.

Record the find interaction in the ToDo session and update all help
transcripts to include the new command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Apply PR review naming and docs fixes
commitResults.messageBody:
Address review feedback on generated task data, Javadoc punctuation, and command naming.

Ignore and remove the runtime task data file, add the missing period to the execute Javadoc, and rename fromInput to parseInput with updated callers and tests. This keeps repository state clean and makes the method name describe its parsing behavior.

The JavaFX interface needs to reuse Plana's command behavior without
coupling the GUI to console input or separators.

Add a reusable Plana response API and make Ui write to an injectable
output stream. Preserve the existing console behavior while exposing
command metadata and response text for GUI chat bubbles. Add tests for
command execution, persistence, errors, and the bye command.

Plana currently exposes only the console entry point, so users cannot interact with the task manager through a graphical interface.

Add a separate JavaFX Launcher and FXML chat window that routes commands through Plana's existing parser, task list, persistence, errors, and bye behavior. Use Plana-specific labels, avatars, colors, and documentation, and keep console UI tests compiling the CLI layer.

The original help response padded commands into two fixed-width columns, causing descriptions to wrap into unrelated lines inside the JavaFX chat bubble.

Format each command and its description on separate indented lines, reduce the bubble font slightly, and update the UI test expectations so the help remains readable across window sizes.
TaskList.add accepts zero or more tasks while preserving the order of existing single-task calls. Add regression coverage for bulk and empty additions so the new API behavior is explicit.
Bring the verified varargs task-list API into the local development branch. Preserve the existing single-task behavior while including the regression coverage for bulk and empty additions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add ASCII banner to GUI introduction
commitResults.messageBody:
The JavaFX window began with only a plain greeting, while the console introduction starts with Plana's wordmark.

Add the compact CLI-style wordmark before the GUI greeting and render that first bubble with a monospaced font so the artwork remains aligned in the responsive chat layout.

commitResults.messageTitle: Restore full banner art in GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
The JavaFX introduction only used the compact wordmark, so the full
decorative bannerArt from the CLI was missing from the GUI.

Share the CLI banner and art through Plana's welcome methods, display
the full artwork before the greeting in its own compact monospaced
bubble, and preserve the CLI startup output.
Give the JavaFX input field a short prompt so users immediately know\nwhere to enter their next task command.

Error responses previously inherited successful command colors, including
the green add-task style for malformed task commands.

Carry explicit error metadata through Plana's response API and display
errors in a restrained rose bubble so failures are easy to distinguish.

The JavaFX stage used a generic title and had no application icon.

Use a friendly task-buddy title and generate a compact green P icon that
matches Plana's existing avatar colors.
